newsitem.title: INDIA: Late rally helps Indian shares end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Late rally helps Indian shares end mixed.

text.p: ** Indian shares finish mixed, late rally helps ** Activity mostly of position-squaring ** Benchmark Bombay share index ends 0.89 points higher at
2,881.15, off 2,850.06 low ** National exchange index loses 2.63 points to 827.25 ** The Delhi index eases 1.15 points to 640.51, Calcutta
Shares across India ended mixed on Friday after a day spent mostly drifting lower following late short covering, brokers said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) closed 0.89 points higher at 2,881.15, after moving between 2,850.06 and 2,893.70.
"The market attracted short-covering towards the close. Otherwise, it was a very dull day," said Mehul Patel, dealer at Mukesh Babu Securities Ltd.
The 50-share National Stock Exchange (NSE) index dropped 2.63 points to 824.62.
The net traded value was 7.46 billion rupees in 35 million shares at the NSE.
Patel said business consisted mostly of position-squaring because it was the last day of weekly account at the BSE.
Traders expect carry-forward charges to stay low as buyers were mostly foreign funds who do not carry-forward trades but take delivery.
"Technically, the market looks ripe for rebound," said one analyst. "But confidence levels are low."
The Delhi index dropped 1.15 points to 646.80 at close after touching the day's low of 640.51.
Bajaj Auto rallied 15.75 rupees to 740 and Gujarat Ambuja Cement 10.50 to 232 on foreign fund buying and scattered short covering, traders said.
ACC firmed 10.50 rupees to 1,010.50, Indian Hotel 13.75 to 675 and Hindustan Ciba 59 to 3,000.
Nestle fell 18.0 rupees to 177, Ranbaxy 4.25 to 520, Hindustan Lever 9.25 to 781, ITC 5.0 to 278.50 and M&M 2.25 to 308.75.
